items.title: Deeply nested expressions abort the process with a stack overflow at compile time
Compiling a `const` with overflowing integer arithmetic panics the compiler
Cycle in import false positive when use -ing a single-component context module (e.g. rune_modules::http)
items.body:
**Description**

Importing a context-installed module whose item path is a *single* root
component (e.g. `::http` from `rune-modules`) with `use http;` produces a
bogus `Cycle in import` compile error — both when the imported name is used
and when it is never used at all. Multi-component imports (`use foo::bar;`)
and fully-qualified paths without `use` work fine.

**Minimal reproduction** (rune 0.14.1 / 0.14.2, rune-modules 0.14.x):

```rust
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut context = rune::Context::with_default_modules()?;
    context.install(rune_modules::http::module(true)?)?;

    let mut sources = rune::Sources::new();
    sources.insert(rune::Source::memory(r#"
use http;

pub fn main() {
    let _ = http::Client::new();
}
"#)?)?;

    // Fails with: Cycle in import
    let _unit = rune::prepare(&mut sources).with_context(&context).build()?;
    Ok(())
}
```

Control cases (same setup):

| Script | Result |
|---|---|
| `use http;` + `http::Client::new()` |  `Cycle in import` |
| `use json;` + `json::from_string("{}")` |  `Cycle in import` |
| `use http;` but never used |  `Cycle in import` |
| no `use`, direct `http::Client::new()` |  compiles |

**Root cause (brief)**

`insert_import` indexes `use http;` at item `::http` with target `::http` —
the entry is self-referential because `at.extended(target.last())` equals the
target for a single-component crate path. When the import is later resolved,
`import()` follows this self-loop and `visited.try_insert` fails on the
second iteration → `ErrorKind::ImportCycle`. The context module meta is never
consulted, because `import_step` only follows context metas of `Kind::Alias`
(context modules are `Kind::Module`).

**Versions affected**: 0.14.0, 0.14.1, 0.14.2, `main` (verified empirically
on 0.14.1/0.14.2 and by code inspection on `main`; the relevant regions of
`query.rs` / `worker/import.rs` are identical).

can't use native function in mod
Trigonometry function support

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
I'm interested in using rune to evaluate some mathematical expressions, and I'm struggling to figure out how to use `sin`, `cos`, etc.

I don't see anything in `rune-modules` that looks like it wraps `core::f64`.

Is it possible to use trig functions in Rune?

```
error: Missing item sin
  ┌─ <memory>:2:1
  │
2 │ sin(x)
  │ ^^^ Missing item sin

Error:
   0: Failed to build rune sources (see diagnostics for details)
```

After a bit more investigation, it actually seems like `rune::modules::f64` is where it would be implemented, and that module is missing the common trig functions.

items.title: Field not available to get on <struct>
Cannot mutate nested field
Can't construct struct with named field
Standard macros should live in the `rune` crate and not `rune-modules`
items.body:
The reason macros live in the `rune-modules` is historical - it used to not be possible to declare macros inside of the `rune` crate. But this is no longer the case.

The old `rune-modules` modules will be deprecated, and a link to this issue set up.

This will be a backwards compatible change, but you are simply encouraged to let these macros be installed through the `rune` crate and [`Context::with_default_modules`](https://docs.rs/rune/latest/rune/compile/struct.Context.html#method.with_default_modules). In a future major release this will otherwise cause breakages.

So if you're installing modules manually like this:

```rust
context.install(&rune_modules::test::module(false)?);
```
You'll have to change it to this:
```rust
context.install(&rune::modules::test::module()?);
```
